title: Residue-Governed Continuation Arrow
purpose: Introduce A ->r B as the first explicit RT continuation-rule notation, defining residue-governed continuation as a process transformation rather than a symbolic rewrite.

canonical_claims.statement: A ->r B means B is the residue-conditioned continuation of A.
The ->r arrow is not a syntactic rewrite operator; it is a governed continuation relation.
Residue r carries irreversible continuation history into the transition from A to B.
A ->r B is admissible only when B preserves lawful continuation from A under residue constraints.

objects.name: Residue-Governed Continuation Arrow
objects.definition: A ->r B denotes that B is a residue-conditioned lawful continuation of A.

objects.name: Residue Continuation Constraint
objects.definition: The historical residue condition constraining admissible continuation.

rules.name: Residue Continuation Rule
rules.reading: A continues into B under residue-governed continuation.

rules.name: Non-Rewrite Constraint
rules.reading: The continuation arrow is process-governed and must not be interpreted as mere symbolic substitution.

rules.name: Residue Preservation Constraint
rules.formal: A ->r B only if r(A) participates in the admissibility of B
rules.reading: The output condition B must remain constrained by the residue inherited from A.

domain_separation.rule: The symbols A and B in A ->r B are generic process states unless explicitly rebound to a specific domain.
domain_separation.meta_domain_guard: A and B in this rule must not be confused with A_meta := δα(ℰ>0) and B_meta := (ℰ≠0).
domain_separation.affect_effect_guard: When applied to A|E, the rule must preserve the affect/effect domain unless a projection operator explicitly changes domain.

validation_requirements: ->r is not described as a syntactic rewrite.
No new primitive object is introduced.
global_validate.py passes or reports only pre-existing hygiene warnings.

next_recommended_patch.title: Governed Continuation Arrow Family
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Generalize ->r into a family of governed continuation arrows such as ->o, ->a, and ->p without collapsing them into syntactic rewrite.

notes: A and B remain generic process states unless explicitly rebound.
The arrow is a process transformation, not a symbolic rewrite.
The residue subscript r carries continuation history into admissible continuation.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
The continuation rule is domain-local and does not alter the canonical RT core.
Sigma_RT remains deferred and is not formalized here.
